1.title: The Plans Practice
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: The Plans Practice. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Explain the purpose of the plans practice and its relationships with the principles. Explain the purpose of the work package description, project product description and plans. Define schedule, dependency, project plan, stage plan, team plan, exception plan and scope. Describe the planning horizon, project stages, product-based planning, tolerances and delivery sustainability. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (sixty percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: Purpose
1.text: Purpose. The plans practice supports communication and control by defining the means of delivering the products: what will be delivered, how, when, by whom and at what cost. A plan is a proposal, baselined once approved.

1.title: Plan levels
1.text: Plan levels. Project plan. The whole project: major products, stages, overall cost, time and quality. Stage plan. One management stage in detail, produced near the stage end for the next stage. Team plan. The plan of a team manager for the work packages (optional). Exception plan. A plan that replaces the current plan when a tolerance would be exceeded; requested by the board.

1.title: Plan levels, continued
1.text: Plan levels. The figure shows this: The levels of plan: project, stage, team and exception.

1.title: Plan levels, continued
1.text: Plan levels. Schedule. The timing of activities and resources. Dependency. An item or activity that must happen before another can start or finish. Scope. The sum of the work (products and activities) to be done.

1.title: Planning guidance
1.text: Planning guidance. Planning horizon. How far ahead you can plan reliably: detail near, outline far. Project stages. The project is divided into management stages; detailed plan for the next stage only. Product-based planning. Plan starting from the products, then the activities needed. Tolerances. The permissible deviation from a plan before escalation (set for time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk, sustainability). Delivery sustainability. Plan so the project delivers in a sustainable way (environment, resources, social effects).

1.title: Product-based planning (the technique)
1.text: Product-based planning (the technique). Write the project product description (what the project must deliver). Create a product breakdown structure (the products as a hierarchy). Write product descriptions for the products. Create a product flow diagram (the order products are built). Then identify activities and dependencies, estimate, schedule, and assess risks. Exam tip: Product first, activities second. If an option says to list activities before knowing the products, it is not product-based planning.

1.title: Management products
1.text: Management products. Project product description. What the project as a whole must deliver, with acceptance criteria. Work package description. The work to be done and the product to deliver, handed from the project manager to a team manager. Plan. Project, stage, team and exception plans. Exam tip: Work package description goes to a team manager. Project product description covers the whole project. Match the product to the audience. Exam tip: An exception plan replaces the current plan; it is not a new, extra plan.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A tolerance is forecast to be exceeded and the board asks for a replacement plan. Which plan is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Exception plan. An exception plan replaces the current plan when a tolerance would be exceeded.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements about plans are C O R R E C T? (one) A stage plan covers one management stage. (two) A project plan covers the whole project. (three) A team plan is required for every project. (four) A dependency is an activity that can start at any time. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and two. Stage and project plans are defined that way.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. blank planning starts from the products and then works out the activities. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Product-based. Product-based planning starts from products.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which management product hands work from the project manager to a team manager? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Work package description. The work package description defines the work and the product.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Why is only the next stage planned in detail? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Because the planning horizon limits how far ahead plans can be reliable. Detail is reliable only near; later stages are in outline.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which describes a dependency? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An item or activity that must happen before another can start or finish. That is a dependency.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the four plan levels. Answer: Project plan, stage plan, team plan and exception plan. Question two. What triggers an exception plan? Answer: A tolerance forecast to be exceeded. Question three. What is the first step of product-based planning? Answer: Write the project product description.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a work package description? Answer: The work to be done and the product to deliver, given to a team manager. Question five. Define scope. Answer: The sum of the work (products and activities) to be done. Question six. What is a planning horizon? Answer: How far ahead you can plan reliably.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Plan levels: project, stage, team, exception. Product-based planning: project product description, P B S, product descriptions, flow diagram. Tolerances: permissible deviation before escalation. Products: project product description, work package description, plan.
